OriginalProposition: Temporary protection (tillfälligt skydd) is an EU protection framework.
FinalProposition: Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/382 activated the EU temporary-protection mechanism under Directive 2001/55/EC.
Notes: Replaced generic label with the exact legal framework and activating instrument.

OriginalProposition: A Swedish residence permit (uppehållstillstånd) is an individual decision under that framework.
FinalProposition: The Swedish Migration Agency decides whether to grant an individual residence permit under the Temporary Protection Directive.
Notes: Narrowed the legal relationship to the deciding authority and individual grant decision.

OriginalProposition: The EU end date does not automatically set the expiry date printed on every Swedish permit or residence-permit card (uppehållstillståndskort).
FinalProposition: The EU protection horizon and Swedish permit validity are distinct: permits decided before 5 August 2026 are stated by the Migration Agency to be valid until 4 March 2027, while the EU scheme runs until 4 March 2028.
Notes: Replaced unsupported universal-card negative with the official cohort dates.

OriginalProposition: Swedish guidance describes Ukrainian nationals, certain people who previously had protection in Ukraine, and specified family members.
FinalProposition: Swedish guidance describes Ukrainian nationals, certain people who previously had protection in Ukraine, and specified family members.
Notes: Current Swedish application guidance lists the covered groups and specified family members.

OriginalProposition: The reviewed Swedish public guidance does not settle every EU-law case involving third-country nationals or stateless people.
FinalProposition: Under Article 2(2) of Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/382, Member States must apply that Decision or adequate national protection to stateless persons and non-Ukrainian third-country nationals who held a valid Ukrainian-law permanent residence permit before 24 February 2022 and cannot return safely and durably to their origin country or region.
Notes: Replaced an unprovable negative about all public guidance with the exact EU-law cohort; claim reopen resolved.

OriginalProposition: examples in guidance are not a universal document checklist.
Notes: Merged into SE-TP-01-C020; its “examples are not a universal checklist” caveat was unsupported and redundant with the narrowed exact examples proposition.

OriginalProposition: Submitting an application is not the same as receiving a residence permit.
FinalProposition: An application is reviewed first; the Migration Agency then sends a decision stating whether a residence permit has been granted or the application rejected.
Notes: Replaced abstract equivalence statement with the official decision sequence.

OriginalProposition: It lists possible evidence such as an exit stamp, Reserv+ e-VOD or other official documents.
FinalProposition: For first-time applicants aged 23–65 subject to the military-obligation rule, the Migration Agency lists an exit stamp, a Reserv+ e-VOD certificate, or other official documents as possible proof.
Notes: Scoped the examples to the precise first-time applicant cohort and rule.

OriginalProposition: The Swedish example is not an EU age band.
FinalProposition: For first-time Swedish applicants aged 23–65, the Migration Agency requires proof of fulfilled Ukrainian military obligations or exemption when the application is made on or after 5 August 2026.
Notes: Replaced unsupported comparison with the exact Swedish age and application-date rule.

OriginalProposition: The reviewed guidance does not settle repeat applications, interrupted protection or every case outside that example.
Notes: Broad negative claim about repeat, interrupted and out-of-example cases was not established; removed rather than imply absence of legal rules.

OriginalProposition: Temporary protection and Swedish population registration (folkbokföring) are different matters.
FinalProposition: The Swedish Tax Agency decides whether a person with a temporary-protection permit meets the population-registration requirements.
Notes: Replaced broad status distinction with the respective competent authorities and decisions.

OriginalProposition: The special rule prevents registration during the first 12 months of combined permit validity.
FinalProposition: For permits granted on or after 1 November 2023, the special registration rule generally bars population registration during the first 12 months of the permit’s combined validity, subject to statutory exceptions.
Notes: Added the rule’s cohort and exception qualification.

OriginalProposition: After that, registration depends on whether regular overnight stays in Sweden are expected for at least another six months and on the other applicable conditions.
FinalProposition: After one year with a temporary-protection permit, expected residence on a permit for at least 18 months from its grant date is required for population registration.
Notes: Used Tax Agency’s current public test rather than shorthand that obscured the calculation.

OriginalProposition: Registration is not automatic after one year.
FinalProposition: Registration is not automatic after one year.
Notes: Tax Agency guidance makes registration conditional and states that it decides individual cases.

OriginalProposition: A coordination number (samordningsnummer) or personal identity number (personnummer) is not a residence permit.
FinalProposition: A coordination number is an identifier for a person who has never been listed in the Swedish Population Register; a personal identity number is assigned to each person who is listed.
Notes: Replaced unsupported comparison with the official definitions and allocation rule.

OriginalProposition: A granted Swedish temporary-protection permit includes work authorization while that permit is valid.
FinalProposition: A person aged 16 or older who has been granted a Swedish residence permit under the Temporary Protection Directive has the right to work in Sweden.
Notes: Added the age threshold and granted-permit condition in the official guidance.

OriginalProposition: A pending application or receipt is not the same as a granted permit.
FinalProposition: A pending application is not a granted permit: the Migration Agency issues a separate decision stating whether the permit is granted or the application rejected.
Notes: Replaced an abstract comparison with the source’s application/decision distinction.

OriginalProposition: Ordinary travel, moving abroad and formally transferring protection are separate events.
FinalProposition: A temporary-protection permit issued by another EU country does not automatically authorize residence in Sweden; a person wishing to live in Sweden must apply to the Swedish Migration Agency.
Notes: Replaced unsupported general comparison of travel, moving and transfer with the official cross-country rule.

OriginalProposition: The official guidance reviewed did not show exact opening dates or booking instructions for that opportunity.
FinalProposition: In September 2026, the Migration Agency said that people whose permit decisions were made before 5 August 2026 would have an opportunity to apply for an extension in early 2027.
Notes: Converted unsupported negative about missing dates into a dated statement of the Agency’s published expectation.

OriginalProposition: The evidence required for an application depends on the applicable procedure.
FinalProposition: The first-time Swedish temporary-protection application requires identity documents.
Notes: Specified the application type and current document requirements.

OriginalProposition: Biometrics requirements depend on the applicable procedure.
FinalProposition: Applicants seeking an extension book a photo and fingerprint appointment in the e-service; first-time applicants are told how to complete biometrics after applying.
Notes: Replaced general conditional wording with the procedure-specific biometric steps.

OriginalProposition: Conditions differ between temporary-protection groups.
FinalProposition: Conditions differ between temporary-protection groups.
Notes: The official guidance enumerates materially different eligibility conditions by cohort.

OriginalProposition: Ukrainian nationality alone does not establish that a person qualifies for temporary protection.
FinalProposition: Ukrainian nationality alone does not establish that a person qualifies for temporary protection.
Notes: The official guidance requires additional conditions beyond Ukrainian nationality.

OriginalProposition: A formal transfer of temporary protection requires consent.
FinalProposition: A formal transfer of temporary protection requires consent.
Notes: Directive 2001/55/EC Article 26(1) expressly makes inter-Member-State transfer subject to consent of the persons concerned.

OriginalProposition: A formal transfer can affect the Swedish temporary-protection permit.
FinalProposition: A formal transfer can affect the Swedish temporary-protection permit.
Notes: Directive 2001/55/EC Article 26(4) provides that the departure-state permit expires and its temporary-protection obligations end on transfer.

OriginalProposition: Some qualifying family applications are also covered.
FinalProposition: Some qualifying family applications are also covered.
Notes: The Migration Agency explains that family members may apply under the specified qualifying alternative permit routes.

OriginalProposition: The effect depends on the permit and the person’s situation.
FinalProposition: Whether a temporary-protection permit holder is covered by the Reception Act depends on population-registration status: a person already registered is not covered by that Act.
Notes: Narrowed the vague “effect depends” claim to the source’s registration-dependent support consequences.

OriginalProposition: It depends on the permit route and its requirements.
FinalProposition: The requirements for an alternative residence permit differ by permit type.
Notes: The Migration Agency states that requirements vary with the requested permit.

OriginalProposition: This is a route-specific example, not a general residence clock for temporary-protection holders.
FinalProposition: Since 11 June 2026, a person holding a Swedish temporary-protection permit may apply from within Sweden for specified work, self-employment, research, higher-education or EU Blue Card permits, if the route requirements are met.
Notes: Replaced vague “route-specific example” language with the exact categories of the limited in-country route.

OriginalProposition: July 2026 guidance also does not clearly settle every temporary-protection category.
Notes: Merged into SE-TP-02-C024, which now states the directly supported scope exclusion in Directive 2003/109/EC.

OriginalProposition: not every type of stay necessarily counts.
FinalProposition: The Migration Agency excludes permits for temporary stays, such as visits or studies below doctoral level, from the five-year residence calculation for Swedish long-term resident status.
Notes: Scoped the proposition to the published residence test and named exclusion category.

OriginalProposition: The reviewed sources do not establish whether earlier time under temporary protection counts after a person changes to another residence basis.
FinalProposition: Directive 2003/109/EC on EU long-term resident status does not apply to people authorized to reside on the basis of temporary protection or awaiting a decision on that status.
Notes: Replaced unresolved speculation about crediting prior TP time after a status change with the Directive’s exact current scope rule.

OriginalProposition: It is not the limited 2026 route for some temporary-protection holders.
Notes: Merged into SE-TP-02-C017; the limited 2026 in-country route is stated there with its exact permit categories.

OriginalProposition: The filing condition does not guarantee continued residence while the case is pending.
FinalProposition: Under Act 2026:456, if the current temporary-protection permit has expired when the application is decided, an alternative permit may be granted only if the application was filed while the current permit was valid.
Notes: Replaced unsupported statement about continued residence pending a decision with the statute’s exact grant condition.
